conflict_topics: moving an open bowl (safety and practicality)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants used concise, realistic time estimates ('four minutes', 'eight minutes') to justify positions.
Physical actions (Robin TAKE_SEAT; Jamie LEAVE_SEAT; Alex TAKE_SEAT) grounded the dialogue and changed incentives.
Some repetition of the same claim (Jamie repeatedly: tissue doesn't give priority; Alex repeats reliance argument) but not excessive.
Casey provided a brief practical observation about aisle narrowing, adding groundedness.
evaluation.final_reason: Jamie finished eating and vacated the seat; Alex then took the seat. The dispute ended when the occupant completed the task and left.
position_change_notes: Jamie: retained the position of not giving up the seat while still eating; then departed once finished (evidence: Turn 10 and LEAVE_SEAT).
Alex: maintained claim to the seat via the reservation rationale and waiting threat, then took the seat once it was vacated (evidence: repeated requests and TAKE_SEAT).
Casey: issued one practical remark about aisle narrowing; no change of position observed.
Robin: took the alternative seat (observable TAKE_SEAT), which altered available options for Alex.

round_scores.evidence: Alex claims the tissue packet was left to reserve the seat and demands Jamie move to sit and eat now. Jamie refuses, saying being already seated and eating gives priority and she won't carry the open bowl. Incompatible claims over who should occupy the disputed seat: Alex's reservation claim vs Jamie's current use.

Two minutes pass with Jamie's bowl still more than half full. Alex offers to wait two more minutes or asks Jamie to stand and leave the bowl (which Jamie rejects for safety). Positions remain incompatible: Alex needs to sit soon, Jamie refuses to move while eating.

After two more minutes Jamie reports about one-third of bowl left and reiterates she needs ~4 minutes and will not stand; Alex emphasizes reliance on the tissue reservation and demands a concrete accommodation. The substantive dispute about who should occupy the seat persists.

A different seat becomes available but Robin takes it (observable action). Alex's alternative is removed, increasing pressure. Jamie still has several spoonfuls left, so the incompatible state persists though Jamie is near finishing.

Jamie announces she's finished and will leave the seat, then physically LEAVE_SEAT; Alex then TAKE_SEAT. The substantive dispute over who occupies the seat is settled by Jamie finishing eating and vacating.
Two minutes later the disputed seat is occupied by Alex, the alternative by Robin, Jamie's bowl is empty, and there are no standing seat-seekers. No substantive disagreement remains.

substantive_insights: Informal reservation signals (tissue packet) create a conflict when they meet a current occupant's ongoing use; norms about priority differ.
Practical safety concerns (open bowl spilling) constrained feasible accommodations (Jamie unwilling to stand and carry bowl).
Third-party actions (Robin taking the other open seat) materially changed Alex's alternatives and escalated urgency.
The dispute resolved through completion of the occupant's activity rather than an interim transfer or enforced concession.
